# URL features 1.0.0

Status: selected specification for a future shared training/inference extractor, 13 November 2026. This document specifies behavior; no extractor is implemented or run by this task. The normative bundle is this document, `feature-schema.json`, `vocabularies.json`, the fixture specification and the pinned reference assets identified in `references/`. It is a deliberately strict RFC-derived URL profile, **not** a WHATWG/browser navigation parser. Acceptance does not establish reachability, ownership, security, label correctness or phishing probability.

## Input and representations

The input is one Unicode string, never a coercion of numbers, nulls or objects. **R** is its exact spelling, measured in Unicode scalar values/code points, without trimming, normalization, global decoding, scheme removal or case folding. Reject surrogate code points, C0 controls U+0000..001F, U+007F..009F, any Unicode White_Space code point (Unicode 17.0 PropList: U+0009..000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000..200A, U+2028..2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000), and literal backslash anywhere. This explicit list, not language-specific `isspace`, is normative. ASCII space is therefore invalid even in a path; percent-encoded space is permitted. Outside the authority, all other Unicode scalar values are permitted, including noncharacters and raw ASCII `<`, `>`, `[`, `]`, `"`, `{`, `}`, `|`, `^` and backtick: this is an explicitly permissive analytical URI/IRI spelling extension, not RFC3986 conformance or browser equivalence. These characters remain lexical spelling and token separators; no escaping repair occurs. The maximum R length is 65,536 code points (inclusive); greater input is unsupported, never truncated. This bound is an engineering limit, not a phishing threshold.

Recognized input forms, in priority order:

1. ASCII-case-insensitive `http://` or `https://`: `source_scheme` is `http` or `https`, `scheme_form=explicit`, `host_recovered=false`.
2. Leading `//`: `source_scheme=null`, `scheme_form=network_path`, `host_recovered=false`.
3. Otherwise, a dotted DNS name (including an authority with UTS46 mapped dot separators U+3002/U+FF0E/U+FF61), strict dotted-decimal IPv4 address, or bracketed IPv6, optionally followed by `:port`, and then path/query/fragment: parse an internal view formed by prefixing **only `//`**; `source_scheme=null`, `scheme_form=absent`, `host_recovered=true`. The prefix is never included in R or any lexical count. `a.test:443` is therefore eligible authority spelling, not an invented scheme. A leading RFC scheme token followed by `:` that cannot be a dotted DNS authority plus decimal port is `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEME`; e.g. `mailto:a.test` and `https:a.test`. Colon-free `a/path` is an invalid host. Relative references and single-label hosts are outside this profile: a nonempty single-label candidate is invalid/INVALID_HOST; leading `/`, `?` or `#` leaves empty authority and is invalid/EMPTY_AUTHORITY under the stated precedence.

Split authority at the first literal `/`, `?` or `#`. Split off the first literal `#` as fragment F, then the first literal `?` before that as query Q; path P is the remaining path spelling (empty or begins `/`). Further `?` are ordinary Q/F characters; further `#` are ordinary fragment spelling under this profile extension, explicitly retained in F. Preserve `query_present` and `fragment_present` separately from empty Q/F. Never remove dot segments or collapse slashes. Within authority, any `@` is rejected (`USERINFO_UNSUPPORTED`); this privacy-conscious profile intentionally does not accept RFC userinfo. An empty authority is invalid. Brackets are valid only as a single whole-host bracketed IPv6 literal, before an optional port. No leading/trailing or repeated empty DNS labels except one trailing root dot are allowed.

`port` is null if absent; otherwise nonempty ASCII decimal digits, numeric value 0..65535 inclusive. Leading zeros are permitted and represented numerically in metadata; R preserves them. A bare colon or signs are invalid. Port 0 is accepted syntax, not a claim that navigation succeeds. Default ports are not removed from R. Unbracketed IPv6, zone identifiers (including `%25zone`), IPvFuture and any percent encoding in the authority host are rejected. Host case and exactly one final root dot are normalized only in H.

**H** is a strict canonical IPv4, RFC 5952 IPv6 (no brackets), or lowercase DNS A-label sequence without its final root dot. IPv6 uses lowercase pure hexadecimal words even for IPv4-embedded addresses (e.g. `::ffff:c000:280`), longest zero run of at least two words compressed, earliest run on ties; no dotted tail in H. A four-label all-numeric spelling must be IPv4: exactly four decimal octets 0..255, no leading zeros except the single digit `0`. An IPv4 source with a trailing dot is invalid/INVALID_IP. Any all-numeric dotted name with another label count is invalid; octal/hexadecimal/short forms are rejected. More precisely, after removing at most one candidate DNS root dot and before IDNA, an authority whose labels are all either ASCII decimal digit runs or `0x`/`0X` followed by ASCII hex digits is an IP candidate; only the strict four-decimal-octet form without a root dot succeeds, otherwise INVALID_IP. A DNS name must have at least two labels and at least one nonnumeric label. Apply Unicode 17.0 UTS #46 revision 35 nontransitional ToASCII, with UseSTD3ASCIIRules, CheckHyphens, CheckBidi, CheckJoiners and VerifyDnsLength true; IgnoreInvalidPunycode false. Thus `faß.de` becomes `xn--fa-hia.de`, not `fass.de`. Valid A-label input is decoded/revalidated/reencoded under the same settings. Normalize mapped dot separators first, permit/remove exactly one final mapped root dot, then verify no empty labels and apply DNS length limits (labels 1..63 ASCII octets and H at most 253). Mapping U+3002/U+FF0E/U+FF61 to dots follows UTS #46, but this cannot turn a syntactically numeric alternative IP into a valid IP: all-numeric or numeric/hex DNS output after mapping is INVALID_IP. DNS Unicode mapping must not bypass the at-least-two-label rule. Unknown suffixes are accepted syntax and carry `suffix_rule='*'`; no DNS lookup occurs.

**Suffix policy:** use the exact offline `references/public_suffix_list.dat`, SHA-256 `b3f2d087e147f5fb4226710acb180d4f2361a281473e234d61005e46afdc8891`, VERSION `2026-11-12_19-44-12_UTC`, COMMIT `aa004f90b4cbe1c54ea96375622eca83d76059f0`. Include both ICANN and PRIVATE sections. Follow the PSL longest-match, wildcard, exception and default `*` algorithm on canonical H, with PSL Unicode rule labels converted under the pinned IDNA policy: remove exception `!` and wildcard `*.` syntax before converting the remaining domain labels, then restore the rule operators. Record `public_suffix`, `registrable_domain`, `suffix_rule`, and `suffix_section` (`ICANN`, `PRIVATE`, `DEFAULT`, or null for IP). Subdomains S are labels preceding the registrable domain; if H itself is a public suffix, registrable_domain is null and S is empty. IP has no suffix/domain/S. This is a feature definition, **not** the final P3 grouping policy. Exact hostnames, ICANN registrable domains, private-aware registrable tenants and organizations are distinct concepts; the selected private-aware field does not establish ownership.

## Encoding and signal views

For accepted inputs, every literal percent in R is a `%HH` escape; however authority errors take precedence: any host percent is HOST_PERCENT_UNSUPPORTED without first validating its escape, userinfo is already rejected, and percent in port is INVALID_PORT. Validate percent grammar in P, then Q, then F: `%` must be followed by two ASCII hex digits; scan left-to-right, consuming a triplet at a time. Only P, Q and F have a signal decoding view: percent-decode once to octets, combine literal Unicode by its UTF-8 encoding, and decode the resulting octets with strict UTF-8. Invalid UTF-8 is an error. Do not recursively decode. `+` stays a plus even in Q; this is RFC URI query spelling, not HTML form submission. Decode **after** structure: `%2F`, `%3F`, `%23`, `%26`, `%3D` never manufacture structural delimiters, query pairs or hosts. Decoded controls/space/backslash may appear in signal views; they are token separators, never reparsed. Keep R and raw P/Q/F unchanged.

ASCII folding means only A..Z→a..z. A token is a maximal nonempty ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9]+` run. Brand and keyword signals use the union of tokens from H and the once-decoded P, Q, F (after ASCII folding). They exclude the scheme and port. Brand-in-subdomain uses those tokens from S labels only; brand-in-path uses decoded P only. Exact token matching prevents `notpaypal` or `paypalish` matching `paypal`; encoded `/%70aypal` does match. This is vocabulary presence, not impersonation or ownership. Punycode token pieces are intentional ASCII spelling signals, not a Unicode confusable detector. Matching entries once is binary per vocabulary item, regardless of occurrences/components.

Nested HTTP text is 1 when any decoded P/Q/F contains ASCII-case-insensitive `http://` or `https://`, with the scheme's first letter at component start or immediately preceded by a non-ASCII-alphanumeric character. No right-host validity or network behavior is inferred. `httpstuff`, `xhttp://` and the original scheme alone do not match. `?u=HTTP%3A%2F%2Fb.test` does. This honest text indicator intentionally does not claim an observed redirect.

## Ordered model features and legacy mapping

All positions remain traceable; the names below are new schema names. Old column names are **aliases for historical comparison only**, never permission to substitute stored CSV values. Every successful result supplies all 37; no extras/missing keys or silent zero fill. Counts are nonnegative signed int64, indicators int64 restricted to 0/1, entropy/ratio IEEE-754 binary64. `len` below means code points; ASCII means the explicitly bounded ranges above. Named vocabularies are the complete literal contents of `vocabularies.json`, not remote/risk/ownership assertions.

| # | New name | Legacy name | Exact definition |
|---:|---|---|---|
|1|raw_length|url_len|len(R), including original scheme and all components|
|2|raw_at_count|@|literal `@` occurrences in R|
|3|raw_question_count|?|literal `?` occurrences in R|
|4|raw_hyphen_count|-|literal `-` occurrences in R|
|5|raw_equals_count|=|literal `=` occurrences in R|
|6|raw_dot_count|.|literal `.` occurrences in R|
|7|raw_hash_count|#|literal `#` occurrences in R|
|8|raw_percent_count|%|literal `%` occurrences in R|
|9|raw_plus_count|+|literal `+` occurrences in R|
|10|raw_dollar_count|$|literal `$` occurrences in R|
|11|raw_exclamation_count|!|literal `!` occurrences in R|
|12|raw_asterisk_count|*|literal `*` occurrences in R|
|13|raw_comma_count|,|literal `,` occurrences in R|
|14|raw_double_slash_count|//|nonoverlapping literal `//` occurrences left-to-right in R; `///`→1, `////`→2|
|15|raw_ascii_digit_count|digits|characters U+0030..0039 in R|
|16|raw_ascii_letter_count|letters|characters A..Z/a..z in R|
|17|explicit_https|https|1 iff observed source_scheme=https; absent scheme never implies HTTPS|
|18|host_is_ip|having_ip_address|1 iff H is validated IPv4 or IPv6|
|19|host_recovered|abnormal_url|1 iff the authority-only `//` parse view was added (form 3); replaces the ambiguous old heuristic|
|20|shortener_exact_host|Shortining_Service|1 iff DNS H exactly equals a shortener entry; subdomains do not qualify|
|21|brand_token_present|phish_has_brand|1 iff any complete brand token occurs in the union signal view|
|22|brand_token_in_subdomain|phish_brand_in_subdomain|1 iff any brand token in S|
|23|brand_token_in_path|phish_brand_in_path|1 iff any brand token in once-decoded P|
|24|host_hyphen_count|phish_hyphen_count|literal hyphens in H, including IDNA A-label hyphens|
|25|host_ascii_digit_count|phish_digit_count|ASCII digits in H (IPv6 hex letters are letters)|
|26|host_length_gt20|phish_long_domain|1 iff len(H)>20, excluding port/brackets/root dot|
|27|subdomains_gt2|phish_many_subdomains|1 iff number of S labels>2|
|28|listed_final_label|phish_suspicious_tld|1 iff DNS final label in frozen label list; IP→0. Does not claim risk|
|29|keyword_distinct_count|phish_keyword_count|number of distinct keyword entries in the union signal view|
|30|nested_http_text|phish_has_redirect|the bounded decoded component text test above|
|31|query_pair_count|phish_param_count|number of nonempty raw Q segments split on literal `&`; preserve repeats, bare keys and blank values. Split each segment on its first literal `=` only for fixture metadata; absent and empty query→0. `a=&a=1&b&=x&&`→4|
|32|raw_percent_triplet_count|phish_encoded_chars|nonoverlapping valid `%HH` triplets in R before decoding; successful inputs make this equal raw_percent_count|
|33|host_character_entropy|adv_domain_ngram_entropy|Shannon character entropy in bits over H, `-Σ (n_c/N) log2(n_c/N)`; no ngrams, no rounding, H includes dots/IPv6 colons|
|34|raw_path_character_entropy|adv_path_entropy|same formula over raw P; empty P→0; a one-character path→0|
|35|raw_ascii_digit_ratio|adv_digit_ratio|slot15/slot1 in binary64; successful R is nonempty|
|36|subdomain_label_count|adv_subdomain_count|number of labels in S under the private-aware pinned PSL|
|37|raw_ascii_token_count|adv_token_count|number of maximal ASCII alphanumeric runs in R, including original scheme, escape digits and port|

Historical >20 and >2 cutoffs remain transparent descriptive features; this task does not assert their utility or select risk thresholds. Brand/keyword/final-label vocabularies are deterministic conventional cues chosen without performance optimization. Their completeness or empirical value is unknown. Alternative scopes, true ngram entropy, Unicode tokens, decoded lexical counts and richer brand ownership signals require another version and future evidence.

## Result schema, failure and precision

A result contains `contract_version='1.0.0'`, the bundle identity, `status` (`ok`, `invalid`, `unsupported`, `internal_error`), `error_code` (null on success), `features` (ordered 37-number array on success, null otherwise), and metadata specified by `feature-schema.json`. Metadata keys always exist; error cases set **every** metadata value null rather than producing partial lexical vectors. Successful metadata is in-memory extraction output, including canonical H/suffix fields. It is not a logging or persistence authorization: production telemetry/persistence must omit/redact host/domain fields in its separately defined record unless independently authorized. An original URL or decoded component must never be serialized in ordinary results/logs. The synthetic fixture worksheet records P/Q/F separately for independent checking, outside the extraction result schema.

Error precedence is deterministic: (1) INPUT_TYPE; (2) EMPTY_INPUT; (3) INPUT_TOO_LONG; (4) INVALID_CODEPOINT (any surrogate anywhere has global precedence over forbidden characters), then FORBIDDEN_CHARACTER; (5) UNSUPPORTED_SCHEME; (6) EMPTY_AUTHORITY; (7) USERINFO_UNSUPPORTED; (8) INVALID_AUTHORITY (brackets, unbracketed IPv6, host/port separator syntax); (9) INVALID_PORT; (10) HOST_PERCENT_UNSUPPORTED; (11) IP_UNSUPPORTED (zones/IPvFuture), INVALID_IP; (12) INVALID_HOST (DNS/IDNA/length/single label); (13) INVALID_PERCENT_ESCAPE in P then Q then F; (14) INVALID_UTF8_ESCAPE in P then Q then F; (15) NONFINITE_OUTPUT/internal result-schema violation→INTERNAL_CONTRACT_ERROR. INPUT_TOO_LONG, UNSUPPORTED_SCHEME, USERINFO_UNSUPPORTED, HOST_PERCENT_UNSUPPORTED and IP_UNSUPPORTED have status unsupported; INTERNAL_CONTRACT_ERROR has status internal_error; all other listed codes have status invalid. IP zone percent therefore receives HOST_PERCENT_UNSUPPORTED before IP_UNSUPPORTED; a literal zone also receives that host-percent code. Examine only enough of later stages to classify the listed stage. No fallback all-zero vector, null-to-zero coercion, NaN, Infinity, clipping, truncation, browser repair or network lookup is allowed. Failure is an explicit unavailable/Unknown extraction state; downstream exclusion/Unknown denominators need the future experiment policy, not a Safe label.

For feature parity require exact integer equality and `abs(actual-expected)<=1e-12+1e-12*abs(expected)` for slots33..35 only; expected ratios and entropy formulas are mathematically normative, fixture decimals are nearest representable approximations. Use binary64 throughout, with JSON decimal round-trip serialization (no four-decimal rounding). Success invariants include slot32=slot8, slot17=0 when source_scheme=null, slot19=`host_recovered`, slot25≤len(H), slot35=slot15/slot1, finite nonnegative numbers, and slot27=(slot36>2). A non-finite output is an internal error even if every other field could be produced. Dependency/PSL/Unicode mismatches fail startup/configuration validation visibly, never silently select a new table.

## Compatibility and amendments

The 37 positions are traceable, not compatible. Slot19 changes meaning; many other scopes, IDNA/IP, PSL, token, query and vocabulary definitions change. **The P2 model must not consume this vector.** A model must bind the exact contract version, feature names/order, reference/vocabulary hashes and implementation identity; any mismatch is an error. Historical artifacts and audits remain immutable. Future implementation/regeneration/retraining require separate authorization, golden conformance and training/runtime parity, plus applicable evaluation-protocol decisions. This resolves feature semantics in D04 only; no score orientation/rounding, threshold, cohort, duplicate/grouping, split or performance decision is silently frozen.

Semantic versioning: any change capable of changing success/failure, metadata semantics or feature values (including Unicode/PSL/vocabulary/limits) increments MAJOR for this feature contract; optional metadata fields that cannot affect behavior may increment MINOR; wording/extra fixture corrections preserving the normative definition increment PATCH. Never edit a released bundle in place: retain it and publish a new directory/version with amendment, rationale, affected slots, fixture deltas, reviewer and checksums. Adding an implementation test that exposes an ambiguous definition requires an explicit amendment before choosing behavior. Hash files as exact UTF-8 bytes; the bundle identity is the SHA-256 manifest of named files assembled by the coordinator. No network refresh at extraction time.

References and alternatives are recorded in `decisions.md` and `references/`; RFC rules constrain the selected profile but do not make its engineering choices universally correct. Neither the stored CSV nor unchanged runtime is ground truth. Prior audit percentages describe its deliberately class/scheme-stratified 12,000-row sample unless appropriately reweighted; equal aggregate counts never establish rowwise intersections. The historical 311 benign groups included an empty-host group with 392,778 benign rows; diagnostic 128,920 benign exact hostnames are not registrable-domain/private-tenant counts.
